sources.subject: ACPG Loveland Letter's of Support; Sunrise to Sunset & SDGE Access Road Use.
sources.body:
Travis LyonChair Alpine Community Planning Group

Good Morning, Travis,

I am requesting copies of the letters of support we recently discussed that were  put before the ACPG board for a successful vote. 

Some Loveland advocates and recreation users have asked me to follow up on these letters of support. Travis, I urgently need you to forward the letters of support to me. These are crucial for our advocacy efforts, especially in light of the support we have garnered from many other community leaders. Please send me, "reply all"  the letters of support for restoring sunrise to sunset and using the maintenance roads in the SDGE Powerlink easement area.

You might benefit from some follow-up I can provide regarding your recent agenda item for Loveland trails proposals: 

Last night, Sweetwater's BOD passed a motion that the 5 Loveland trails proposal items you reviewed will make up the work plan management will send to the California funding and work oversight group, the Department of Water Resources (DWR). Please see the image below for a rough version of the site plan. 

Travis, your continued involvement and the momentum we (the community) have created, including the commitment of  $75,000 for the master plan, are crucial for the success of the Loveland project. Your efforts will serve our communities on recreation and help defend Loveland wildlife and our lake user neighbors and friends in the face of potential bad ideas and acts against them by the Sweetwater Authority. We have seen the impact of such disasters in the past year, and your support and that of the ACPG is invaluable. 

Best regards,

Russell

> travislyonacpg@gmail.com>, Cherry Diefenbach <csdiefenbach@sbcglobal.net>,
> Sandra Farrell, <tovcsg.chair@gmail.com>, Rebecca Falk <rebfalk7@gmail.com>,
> <petersonenv@hotmail.com>, Jennifer Haider <jennehaider@gmail.com>
>
>
> *SANDAG Board Actions and Discussions - March 2024*
>
> *SANDAG Retreat 2024:*
> March 8th meeting - a Board Retreat held at the Salt Drift Pointe, 536
> 13th Street, Imperial Beach from 8:30 to 3:30. Both the APG Representative
> (Robin Maxson) and Alternate (Eileen Delaney) attended and participated in
> the team building activities. The goal of the Retreat was to build a
> regional planning mindset for the Board members and to develop a set of
> criteria/traits for the next SANDAG CEO. Recruiting and interviewing has
> narrowed the candidate field to six individuals.
>
> *Caltrans:*
> Roy Abboud and Mario Orso - communicated to the APG Rep that Caltrans had
> 2.6 billion in funding for the unincorporated area projects. Also, that
> they would be "speeding up" projects on the SR 67.
>
> *125 Toll Road Action Plan:*
> March 22nd Meeting - Coleen Clementson reported that SANDAG had signed the
> contract with the group (unnamed) that would be running the new back-office
> system and that it would be up and running by the end of the year.
> Independent Performance Auditor - Courtney Ruby will be presenting the
> results of the audit at the next Board meeting. (As it turned out a Special
> SANDAG Board meeting was called for March 29th to specifically discuss the
> results of this internal audit.)
> Report on options discussed with South Bay leaders for early pay off of
> 125 Toll Road would be brought forth in a future meeting.
>
> March 29 Special Board Meeting - The report from the Office of the
> Independent Performance Auditor released a report on March 25th resulted in
> a Special meeting of the Board to be called.  This report was previously
> sent to APG members in a separate email, but here is the link:
> https://www.sandag.org/-/media/SANDAG/Documents/PDF/about/office-of-the-independent-performance-auditor/reports-and-documents/sr-125-investigation-report-final.pdf
>
> The report revealed ongoing, egregious lack of oversight and a pattern of
> failure to take action to correct a multitude of issues with operation of
> the 125 Toll Road.
> Board members questioned every aspect contributing to this situation:
> Why wasn't the Board informed of the back-office discrepancies in tolls
> collected and toll user accounts?
> Why have we signed a contract with the same company that did not deliver
> on the contractual requirements?
> Why would we contract again with companies that did not collect nor record
> tolls correctly?
> What is the criteria for selecting a company for the contract?
> Why wasn't it reported to the Board that tolls stopped being collected due
> to equipment disconnect sooner?
> Why is SANDAG using QuickBooks for accounting purposes?
> Who in SANDAG's executive leadership knew of these issues and when?
> What is SANDAG's Whistle Blower policy?
> Why did SANDAG allow a culture of intimidation to exist with respect to
> the former CEO?
> Why were financial reports repeatedly corrected and the issues leading to
> faulty numbers not corrected instead?
> How much money has the contractor been paid for the 125 Toll Road and for
> other projects they manage, for example the I-15 managed lanes.
> How can we ensure that the same accounting issues have not occurred with
> the I-15?
> How much money in tolls was lost overall?
>
> Board member comments were:
> "After I pick up my jaw from the floor I have a few questions."
> "This isn't just a black eye for SANDAG, but two black eyes."
> "We need to investigate potential fraud."
> "We need to rebuild trust in SANDAG."
>
> The Independent Performance Auditor's recommendations were accepted by the
> Board and more Board actions and answers to questions and concerns would be
> forthcoming at the April 12th regular Board meeting.
>
> *Report of SANDAG's Draft Fiscal Year 2025 Budget Program - Capital
> Projects:*
> SANDAG reported on the DRAFT FY 2025 Budget. The presentation included the
> project and funding allocation of both TransNet and non-TransNet funded
> projects. The hand out (see attachment) was a visual overview of the
> projects and location - Note the lack of projects planned (funded) in the
> unincorporated area of the County. Based on this discrepancy in funding for
> the unincorporated area and for areas of North County the Board heard many
> complaints from its own members.
>
> APG comment to Board: "Good morning. Thank you. Representing the
> unincorporated area where we're 500 thousand strong. I understand that we
> use the limited funds where it can do the most good. But I would like to
> remind everyone to keep in mind that we do have a large population outside
> of the populated corridor. And, that in addition to the 500 thousand, we do
> have thousands of visitors on the weekends. So, I see a lot of funding for
> bikeways which is good for health and greenhouse gas reduction. But I see
> very limited funding for our Vision Zero Plan to reduce highway severe
> injuries and fatalities. I don't see a lot of money in the unincorporated
> area where all of the visitors are coming on the weekends and where there
> is a tremendous amount of pressure on those roadways. Also, I don't see
> that a priority is being given to wildfire evacuation. And, with two
> unsuccessful wildfire evacuations in '03 and '07 it is not a matter of if;
> but when we will have another one. Right now it is green, but it won't be
> that situation in June. I would like to know how SANDAG determines the
> funding allocation - how do they decide that balance between a population
> that is concentrated and a population that is spread out? Yet there is
> still a need in both areas. And, I do appreciate all of your work, but I
> want to understand how that calculus is made. Thank you."
>
> Susan Huntington (SANDAG staff) response: The annual budget really looks
> toward the Regional Plan prioritization process. So the Regional Plan is
> our long term plan and it establishes the implementation schedule of the
> projects. We use multiple different criterias in that project
> prioritization process. The annual budget looks at when those projects are
> meant to be open; like if a project is meant to be open in 2035 we need to
> get started on that project in say 2025. So, we're really looking to
> implement the Regional Plan as we pull the budget together. And, all of
> those criteria for prioritization come through the Regional Plan process."
>
> You can also view my comment at the meeting link:
> https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=arKeg7IFk7w   02:06:30
> and here is the link to the budget document:
> https://www.sandag.org/-/media/SANDAG/Documents/PDF/funding/budget/sandag-program-budget-fy-2025.pdf#page=6
>
> *SANDAG's Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA):*
> Report on RHNA from Sacramento's Housing and Community Development (HCD)
> staff Megan Kirkeby and Marisa Prasse.
> The HCD reported that future development continued to be focused on
> population corridors and not near open spaces or places without
> transportation options. This effectively eliminates rural and semi-rural
> areas for housing.
> Board discussion on the increased legislation from Sacramento (SB 35 and
> SB 423) that punished/fined cities for not meeting their RHNA numbers.
> Cities reported that Sacramento was applying a state-wide housing solution
> to individual cities instead of allowing a more reasonable and attainable
> allocation to be made regionally as some communities had more buildable
> land available than others.  Some unincorporated communities are located
> near job centers and should not be dismissed as potential housing locations
> due to a lack of public transit options.
>
> *APG Update:*
> In addition to this SANDAG report the APG has received acceptance of our
> Associate membership (non-voting) invitation to Community Sponsor Groups by
> Bonsall (Jennifer Haider), Jacumba (Cherry Diefenbach) and Twin Oaks Valley
> (Joseph Bunn). We will formally accept their membership at our June 1st APG
> meeting. Welcome to Bonsall, Jacumba and Twin Oaks Valley!
>
> Report Submitted by:
> Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
> Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
>

    On Thursday, April 25, 2024 at 03:33:51 PM PDT, Travis Lyon <travislyonacpg@gmail.com> wrote:

 Mr. Walsh,
The planning group took 2 actions at last month's meeting related to Loveland Reservoir.
   - We voted to support the 5 projects proposed by Sweetwater Authority to be funded by the $750,000 in funds awarded by the State of California.  

   - We voted to authorize the chair to draft letters of support for Sunrise to Sunset for trail users at Loveland Reservoir.

Tonight the group will vote to approve the two above items as part of the approval of the meeting minutes.  I am still drafting letters of support for Sunrise to Sunset and they have not yet been sent out.
The planning group discussed taking an official position on expanded trail use on SDGE easements, but did not take action on that proposal.
There are no items on tonight's agenda related to Loveland Reservoir.  I too have a family and am currently addressing a medical emergency.  I am not sure if I will be at the meeting tonight, but I wanted to provide you with this update before you made the trip to the meeting.
I expect to send out letters of support for sunrise to sunset very soon.  I appreciate all your efforts to support Loveland Reservoir trail users.
Thank you,
Travis Lyon | ChairAlpine Community Planning GroupP.O. Box 1419, Alpine, CA 91903-1419619.952.8607travislyonacpg@gmail.com

sources.subject: Re: Sunrise to Sunset Discussion at Alpine Community Planning Group.
sources.body:
Steve HalesDirector Friends of Loveland Reservoir

Hello Steve,

Steve, I want to express my sincere gratitude to you and your board for the commendable actions you've taken in support of Sunrise to Sunset. Your efforts have not gone unnoticed and are greatly appreciated. 

Have you reached out to Congressman Issa? Our easement is primarily a federal issue, and while we need follow-through, and community support everywhere we can get it, Congressman Issa is our strongest ally where the Forest Service is concerned. Please ask your board to promote a quality petition for progress on the restoration of  Sunrise to Sunset access ASAP.  As you said recently, agencies like to work with and respond to groups like Friends of Loveland Reservoir. If you need help, please let me and others know, perhaps via membership and a website.  

Your help at the ACPG is important:The ACPG has been a good base at times for Loveland Advocacy but there have been let downs too. Your board members know that  I went to a half dozen meetings with the Alpine Community Planning group for help with Loveland in the year before it was drained and to many meetings since. In the spring of 2022 a strong vote passed by ACPG to encourage Sweetwater to come to the Alpine Group. There was a least one previous resolution to write letters of support on recreation themes.  However, the chair did not complete these tasks despite the strong votes. The same thing appears to be happening with April's nearly unanimous vote for a letter of support from the ACPG on the Sunrise to Sunset. I believe you are aware through CC'd email on this trajectory. We need to work together so the ACPG honors community work and interests at Loveland and the work of the people on the planning advisory board itself on behalf of Loveland Reservoir so we can have success on Sunrise to Sunset and full defense of future complete dewatering which are here. We all agree that land use organizations are falling short of legal easement adherence and should be advised and strenuously petitioned to do otherwise. 

Please check your emails from me about Sweetwater's goal to float 200 acres of solar panels at Sweetwater Reservoir. 

The minimum water levels to float that industrial-type project will likely come from Loveland Reservoir and create new cyclical dewatering episodes. Sweetwater refuses to remove the threat, which is a factor. The good news is that it is being challenged locally in South Bay and here by us. 

Appreciatively,

Russell

Russell Walsh

4639 Montiel Truck Trail

Jamul CA, 91935

    On Wednesday, June 19, 2024 at 10:56:14 AM PDT, Steve Hales <steve@hales.xyz> wrote:

 <!--#yiv3880236540 filtered {}#yiv3880236540 filtered {}#yiv3880236540 filtered {}#yiv3880236540 filtered {}#yiv3880236540 filtered {}#yiv3880236540 p.yiv3880236540MsoNormal, #yiv3880236540 li.yiv3880236540MsoNormal, #yiv3880236540 div.yiv3880236540MsoNormal {margin:0in;font-size:12.0pt;font-family:"Aptos", sans-serif;}#yiv3880236540 a:link, #yiv3880236540 span.yiv3880236540MsoHyperlink {color:#467886;text-decoration:underline;}#yiv3880236540 p.yiv3880236540ydpe1f3a1e6yiv8508440490msonormal, #yiv3880236540 li.yiv3880236540ydpe1f3a1e6yiv8508440490msonormal, #yiv3880236540 div.yiv3880236540ydpe1f3a1e6yiv8508440490msonormal {margin-right:0in;margin-left:0in;font-size:12.0pt;font-family:"Aptos", sans-serif;}#yiv3880236540 span.yiv3880236540EmailStyle21 {font-family:"Aptos", sans-serif;color:windowtext;}#yiv3880236540 .yiv3880236540MsoChpDefault {font-size:10.0pt;}#yiv3880236540 filtered {}#yiv3880236540 div.yiv3880236540WordSection1 {}-->
Hi Russell,

  

FOLR supports honoring the easement terms including sunrise to sunset.  We press for it when we meet with the Forrest Service or with the Sweet Water Authority.  While some progress is being made on many issues, we have had about as much success as you have in getting them to honor that commitment.

  

I’ll bring up the ACPG letter at the next FOLR board meeting.  Of course you can also contact the ACPG directly and ask yourself. 

  

Steve

  

From: Russell Walsh <russellwalsh2003@yahoo.com>
Sent: Tuesday, June 18, 2024 12:23 PM
To: Karen Wood <karensdrealestate@gmail.com>; Steve Hales <sandiegosteve@outlook.com>; Steve Hales <Steve@hales.xyz>
Cc: Don Miller <cadeerhunter@gmail.com>; David Thomas <higherglassdave@gmail.com>; John Allen <jallen8@outlook.com>; Jesus Arreola <jesusarreola226@gmail.com>; Travis Lyon <travislyonacpg@gmail.com>; Smith Kyle - FS CA <kyle.smith4@usda.gov>; Christopher Mika <christopher.mika@mail.house.gov>; Miriam Raftery <editor@eastcountymagazine.org>; Michael Cederwall <mikeycederwall@yahoo.com>; Nicholas Brust <nicholas.brust@sen.ca.gov>; Carolyn McGavock <cmcgavoc@gmail.com>; Kim <dudziktaz@cox.net>; Darlene Cossio <dcossio@sdgoodwill.org>; Bob Kilpatrick <bubba4647@gmail.com>; Andrew Hayes <andrew.hayes@sen.ca.gov>; Maggie Sleeper <maggie.sleeper@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Subject: Re: Sunrise to Sunset Discussion at Alpine Communiity Planning Group.

  

Steve Hales

Director Friends of Loveland

CC Karen Wood Executive Director Friends of Loveland

  

  

Steve,

  

I am following up on your letter from April regarding FOLR support for Sunrise to Sunset at Loveland Reservoir.

As we near the point of longest day length in the summer of 2024 I am curious as to progress made, or effort given for our nature viewer and other recreation users on this matter. 

  

Also, I have advised you about how Sweetwater Authority is a constant applicant and recipient of State and Federal grants, yet is comfortable shortchanging taxpayers and citizens on even the limited sunrise to sunset access to Loveland's shoreline. You told me that FOLR supports that. How can we work together to challenge this taxpayer inequity so that FOLR followers and all other lake users may experience the therapeutic recreation and sometimes food aquistion rights they own at  Loveland Reservoir.

  

Thank you for you work for  nature lovers , fishers and hikers who need this recreation and proper voice and action in our communities by our leaders. I have letters of support on Sunrise to Sunset from Supervisor Anderson if you can use that in you advocacy. The ACPG was almost unaniously in favor of a letter of support to Sweetwater and the Forest Service on Sunrise to Sunset a few months ago, with the FOLR member being the only one to abstain. However , it appears the Chair has not notified or responded to concerns about the creation and issue of that letter. Please follow up on that with Chair Travis Lyon. 

  

Russell Walsh

  

4639 Montiel Truck Trail

Jamul CA, 91935

619-922-6235

  

On Friday, April 12, 2024 at 03:33:03 PM PDT, Steve Hales <steve@hales.xyz> wrote:

  

  

Russell,

 

The FOLR board supports sunrise to sunset hours at Loveland.

 

You are incorrect about what happened at the ACPG meeting.  In Darlene’s position as a member of the ACPG board, she abstained from voting on the motion – but she did not vote “No” or try to “block” it as you say.  And she abstained only after it was obvious the motion would pass anyway.

 

Regardless, Darlene can vote however she likes as a member of the ACPG board, without FOLR approving or justifying that vote. 

 

I hope this clarifies the misunderstanding.

 

Steve

FOLR

 

From: Russell Walsh <russellwalsh2003@yahoo.com>
Sent: Friday, April 12, 2024 7:58 AM
To: Karen Wood <karensdrealestate@gmail.com>; Steve Hales <sandiegosteve@outlook.com>; Steve Hales <Steve@hales.xyz>
Cc: Don Miller <cadeerhunter@gmail.com>; David Thomas <higherglassdave@gmail.com>; John Allen <jallen8@outlook.com>; Jesus Arreola <jesusarreola226@gmail.com>; Sean Walsh <walshsean63@gmail.com>; Travis Lyon <travislyonacpg@gmail.com>; Smith Kyle - FS CA <kyle.smith4@usda.gov>; Christopher Mika <christopher.mika@mail.house.gov>; Miriam Raftery <editor@eastcountymagazine.org>; Michael Cederwall <mikeycederwall@yahoo.com>; Nicholas Brust <nicholas.brust@sen.ca.gov>; Carolyn McGavock <cmcgavoc@gmail.com>
Subject: Sunrise to Sunset Discussion at Alpine Communiity Planning Group.

 

 

 

Karen Wood

Executive Director 

Friends of Loveland Reservoir

Alpine CA

 

Hello  Karen,

 

Thank you for your recent complimentary work on the Loveland fishing float platform and other items of concern for Loveland Lake users. 

 

During the Alpine community planning group meeting last week, a significant issue regarding access to Loveland Reservoir was raised. Your board member, Darlene Cossio,  who is also on the planning group board, attempted to block the group's motion for a letter of support  to Sweetwater Authority and the US Forest Service for sunrise-to-sunset access. She claimed that the issue was already being addressed.

 

Would you please clarify what your board members' actions and comments mean for restoring access at Loveland according to the easement? Why does your board member see this being resolved so that she would block a letter of support and make the statements I am asking about?

 

Another spring and summer of afternoon and early evening recreation at Loveland is slipping away from working people and their families. Please support independent advocates in requesting that the ACPG bring the Cleveland National Forest administrators back to the ACPG meeting for a public follow-up on our meeting with them at the ACPG  last October. 

 

Appreciatively,

 

Russell

request_text:
Re: Public Records Act Request

Dear Alpine Community Planning Group Members,

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I am writing to request a copy of the records detailed below.

I am researching how the Alpine Community Planning Group (ACPG) conducts its business on the part of the residents of Alpine in preparation for publication of an expose. To that end, I request the following records:

1. All Alpine Community Planning Group Agendas and Minutes from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025.

2. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and another member(s) of the Alpine Community Planning Group from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

3. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and another government agency, including between the group members and the County of San Diego from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

4. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and any member of the public, including between the group members and individuals/entities with business before the group from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

Please note that the Public Records Act allows a member of the public to request records by describing their content, rather than asking for specific documents by name; an agency that receives such a request must “search for records based on criteria set forth in the search request.”

Public records represent “any handwriting, typewriting, printing, photostating, photographing, photocopying, transmitting by electronic mail or facsimile, and every other means of recording upon any tangible thing any form of communication or representation, including letters, words, pictures, sounds, or symbols, or combinations thereof, and any record thereby created, regardless of the manner in which the record has been stored.” (Government Code section 7920.545.)

1. This request applies to all records in your agency’s possession, including documents created by a member of another government agency or a member of the public.

2. If specific portions of any documents are exempt from disclosure, please provide the non-exempt portions.

3. Please provide entire documents, even if only parts of them are responsive to this request.

If you maintain records or data in electronic format, please provide them in that same format.

1 California First Amendment Coalition v. Superior Court, 67 Cal.App.4th 159, 165-66 (1998).
2 See California State University v. Superior Court, 90 Cal. App. 4th 810, 824-25 (1999).
3 Gov’t. Code § 6253(a). versions are acceptable) to avoid copying costs.
4 If you are unable to reproduce electronic records in electronic form, please provide a reason for doing so.

I request that you waive copying fees because I have limited resources, and the information requested will be used in the public interest to further the public’s understanding of the local community planning group action. None of the information obtained will be sold or distributed for profit. If you are unable to waive the copying fees, and you anticipate that these costs will exceed $50, or that the time needed to copy the records will delay their release, please contact me so that we can arrange to inspect the document or decide which documents we wish to have copied. Otherwise, please copy and send them as soon as possible. Please respond to this request within ten (10) days, either by providing all the requested records or by providing a written response setting forth the legal authority for withholding or redacting any document and stating when the documents will be made available.

If you require any clarification in identifying responsive documents or focusing this request, please contact [redacted]. Please send all records responsive to this request to Louis Russo.

Thank you for your time and attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

[redacted]

Gov’t. Code §§ 6253(c), 6255.
